title: Boyhood on a Kentucky plantation watching hired hands
summary: He learned singing and dancing by watching Black farm hands, and recalls his brother Richard offering him money to sing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Lee, would you tell a little bit how you, when you were a boy at home, how you watched the hired hands, the colored held hands?

Oh, yes. On the plantation in Kentucky when I was a boy. I was born and raised in a plantation in Kentucky. We had help working around our hired hands. And I used to watch the colored people jump around and dance and sing. And I learned a lot by just watching the hired hands and I'd get ideas from them. And when I was quite a small child, I remember my brother, Richard, he and his buddy came home one day and they wanted me to sing. And I don't, I was so small, I don't remember ever singing. I didn't know what I was going to sing. So they offered me a nickel to sing and I wouldn't take it. So they offered me a dime and I wouldn't take it. So they offered me a quarter and I don't know whether I sing or not. I'm too little, I was too little, I don't remember that part.
